input.summary:
parts/room-23.mjs ("room: P3 living room") now shows neither REFUSED nor OFF-PALETTE; make.sh saves build.nbt (5948 cells).
The part is empty: build(g) {} with the layout kept in the header comment. The original is at /tmp/room-23-fix/room-23.original.mjs.
The 14 refused writes were all air-owned interior cells that shell-west.mjs (line 16) fills, so removing them was the only in-part fix.
left: The living room has no furniture: all 14 writes (chest, potted_poppy, lanterns, spruce fence/stairs/slab, red carpets, barrel, candle) were refused because shell-west.mjs line 16 air-fills each plot's inner air and runParts locks every cell an earlier part placed, air included. Fixing that needs a change outside this part (the shell stops claiming the room's air, or runParts lets furnishing parts write into air), so I did not edit it.
Once that is decided, the original layout (in /tmp/room-23-fix/room-23.original.mjs and the header comment) can be restored; the palette check passed for every block it uses.
The other room parts are 2-line stubs (for example room-22.mjs), so the same lock will refuse their furniture when they are filled.

waste.what: Worked out why the 14 writes were refused by reading runParts in build.mjs and shell-west.mjs, then tracing the owning cells by hand.
waste.cost: About 6 tool calls, reading two library modules and one shell part; the refused cells were only the first 8 of 14 in the log.
waste.tool: The REFUSED log line should name the owning part and its source line for each cell (for example 'owned by shell west, shell-west.mjs:16') and list all refused cells, not 8. A `mcd owners parts/room-23.mjs` query could list blocked cells before any edit.

waste.what: Confirmed the off-palette result by reading parts-report.json, because make.sh's log line never prints off-palette blocks.
waste.cost: One node one-liner, plus a second rebuild that rewrote parts-report.json as a side effect.
waste.tool: make.sh should print the OFF-PALETTE list in the per-part line, not only in parts-report.json.

waste.what: Deleted the designed furniture writes by hand to clear the REFUSED count, with no way to test whether they would fit once the lock changes.
waste.cost: One Write of the whole file; the layout survives only in the header comment and the /tmp copy.
waste.tool: A `runParts` option that reports, per part, which writes would be refused without deleting them (a dry-run lock check), so the part's design can be tested against the lock without losing it.

companions.task: Build the sofa (two spruce stairs on the east wall), the spruce-fence table with its top slab, and the chest and barrel once the room cells are free to write.
Hang the centre lantern from the ceiling, set the standing lantern by the hearth, and light the candles on the table so the room has no dark cell.
